summary.one_liner: bloop is a desktop app that lets you ask natural-language questions about your code, run regex and symbol search, and generate patches using your codebase as context.
summary.what_it_does: bloop provides AI-based conversational search over your repositories, so you can ask questions in plain English and get answers grounded in your code. It includes Code Studio, an LLM playground that uses your code as context. It also offers regex search, symbol search for functions, variables or traits, and query filters to narrow results. Code navigation (go-to-definition and go-to-reference) is built on Tree-sitter for 10+ popular languages. Local and GitHub repositories can be synced, and semantic search uses on-device embeddings. The app is built with Tauri, with search indexes powered by Tantivy and Qdrant.
use_cases: Explain how a file or feature works in simple language
Ask questions about a codebase written in English from another language
Find where a function, variable or trait is defined or used
Search code with regex and filters
Understand poorly documented open source libraries
Reduce code duplication by finding existing functionality
how_to_run: Download the app and follow the onboarding steps (simplest option)
To build from source: clone the repo and check out the oss branch
Create local_config.json at the top-level of the repo with github_access_token and openai_api_key
Follow the build instructions in the repo's build-from-source documentation
notable: Conversational code search and Code Studio LLM playground that use your own code as context
Tree-sitter-based go-to-definition and go-to-reference for 10+ languages
Built from source, it runs with your own OpenAI API key and sends no telemetry
caveats: Building from source requires git-lfs and a local_config.json with API credentials
Index problems may require wiping the bloop cache and reindexing
Building from source uses the oss branch, and the README does not describe the default branch's behavior
